brief.headline: Aluminium's curve tightened on the same session that zinc's and copper's fell apart - it was the only metal on the exchange board whose forward structure firmed, its premium for prompt metal tripled on completely unchanged warehouse stock, and the price closed at a four-week high.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. The exchange settled aluminium at $3,325.00 a tonne on Tuesday, up $15.00 or 0.45%, the highest settlement since 10-August and now only $2.50 below that level. The three-month contract rose $11.00 to $3,319.00, its own highest since 11-August. The move is small in absolute terms but it completes a three-session advance and puts the metal at the top of its four-week range.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE. The gap between the cash price and the three-month price - what the market will pay to have metal now rather than later - TRIPLED, from $2.00 to $6.00, and it did so while the amount of metal sitting in exchange warehouses did not move by a single tonne. For weeks this page has made the opposite point: that record-low inventory was not producing any willingness to pay for prompt metal. That criticism is now partially answered. The honest scale check is that $6.00 on a $3,325 metal is still under two-tenths of one percent - a signal, not a squeeze.

THE CROSS-METAL PICTURE INVERTED IN ONE SESSION, AND THIS IS THE REAL NEWS. Yesterday zinc and copper were paying $182.00 and $92.00 for prompt metal and aluminium was paying $2.00. Today zinc's premium collapsed to $106.00 and copper's to $32.00, while aluminium's rose. Aluminium was the ONLY metal on the board whose forward structure tightened. One session does not make a trend, but the comparison that was unflattering to aluminium for three weeks has reversed.

WHAT TO WATCH. Warehouse stock has now been pinned at exactly 244,525 tonnes for three consecutive published sessions - it is neither draining nor building, and until that changes the record-low inventory figure is a floor under the price rather than a reason for the next leg up. Two interest-rate decisions land inside a week (Europe on Thursday, the United States next Wednesday) and both now carry tightening risk, which is a headwind for a dollar-priced metal. Oil above $98 and rising on Middle East escalation cuts both ways: it raises the cost of making and shipping the metal at the same time as it threatens the supply.

lme.commentary: THE 08-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL PUT CASH AT $3,325.00, UP $15.00 OR 0.45% ON MONDAY'S $3,310.00 AND THE HIGHEST CASH SETTLEMENT SINCE 10-AUGUST - now just $2.50 below that session's $3,327.50. Three-month rose $11.00 to $3,319.00, its highest since 11-August, so cash settled $6.00 ABOVE the forward and THE BACKWARDATION TRIPLED from $2.00. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE HIGHER CASH SETTLEMENT and a cumulative $32.50 advance from Friday. THE STRUCTURE IS THE STORY RATHER THAN THE PRICE. A $6.00 backwardation is the widest since 10-August and it breaks a six-session stretch in which the front of the curve sat within $2.00 of flat. It widened against exchange stock that did not move by a single tonne - the second consecutive published change of exactly zero and the third consecutive reading at 244,525 tonnes. A curve paying more for prompt metal with no warehouse response is being bid by demand for units rather than by an inventory shift, and that is the first such evidence in this fifteen-session window. THE CROSS-METAL COMPARISON THAT HAS EMBARRASSED ALUMINIUM FOR THREE WEEKS INVERTED IN A SINGLE SESSION AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT OBSERVATION ON THE PANEL. Yesterday zinc carried a $182.00 backwardation and copper $92.00 while aluminium paid $2.00, and this page argued that was the cleanest available evidence that aluminium's thirty-six-year inventory low was not translating into prompt scarcity. TODAY ZINC'S BACKWARDATION COLLAPSED TO $106.00 - cash fell $47.00 while three-month ROSE $29.00, with 2,275 tonnes delivered in, the largest zinc build of the window - AND COPPER'S COLLAPSED TO $32.00, because although copper cash rose $197.00 to a window high of $14,737.00, three-month rose $257.00, more. Nickel's contango narrowed $10.00 to $145.00 on a 264-tonne build; lead's contango WIDENED to $47.00 while shedding 3,400 tonnes, the heaviest draw on the board. ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY METAL ON THE BOARD WHOSE CURVE TIGHTENED. THE HONEST QUALIFICATIONS ARE KEPT IN VIEW: $6.00 on $3,325 is eighteen-hundredths of one percent, the August average spread was a $1.60 contango, and one session is not a regime. THE MOVE IS METAL RATHER THAN CURRENCY - the LME's own EUR/USD fixing eased from 1.16230 to 1.16140, a marginally FIRMER dollar, so the advance was made against a small currency headwind rather than helped by a tailwind. THE SOURCE STATE IS CLEAN: both overviews and all five per-metal tables carry 08-September and agree, so no row required reconciliation for the first time in over a month.

drivers.text: Q4-2026 producer offers are public and 18-22% below the Q3 record, and a seventh consecutive search returned no newer dated report — Reuters reported on 02-September-2026, citing four sources involved in the quarterly talks, that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered Japanese buyers $310-$325 per tonne for October-December shipments, down 18% to 22% on the Q3 settlement of $395, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. Talks began the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later this month. Nothing dated later than that report has printed publicly, so the pending range on this page stays at $290-325 rather than being tightened toward either party's number.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM, 02-Sep-2026 - aluminium producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums

drivers.text: The spot-versus-contract gap already implies the reset - the Q4 offers are arithmetic, not a surprise — Spot CIF Japan was last publicly assessed at $370 per tonne against a contracted Q3 settlement of $395, so the quarter was contracted $25 ABOVE where the market has since been clearing. That is precisely the kind of gap a quarterly benchmark closes at the next settlement, which is why a downward reset was the expected outcome rather than the surprising one. The open question is only the size, and the published bid-offer spread between $300 and $310 is the honest measure of the remaining uncertainty.
drivers.source: Platts/periodic public assessments as carried on the premium panel of this page; Reuters via MINING.COM 02-Sep-2026 for the offer range

drivers.text: The producers' stated rationale weakened this session for the first time since the offers were reported — The published justification for the lower Q4 offers was a positive progress report on Middle East production together with softer premiums in Europe. Both legs looked weaker on the 08-September session. Crude rose to a three-month high with Brent above $98 on renewed US-Iran escalation, which is the opposite of progress toward restored Gulf supply, and the exchange curve TIGHTENED rather than loosened - aluminium's backwardation tripled to $6.00 and it was the only metal on the board whose structure firmed. This does not change the offer range, which is a dated public number, but it does weaken the argument behind it.
drivers.source: Trading Economics - aluminium commentary and cross-asset macro board read at this compile (Brent, WTI, three-month crude high, US-Iran escalation)

drivers.text: The North American corridor is now taxed in both directions and the effect will show up in assessments rather than in the exchange price — Canada's counter-tariffs took effect on 08-September-2026 and explicitly include aluminium: counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium rose from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives. The US Section 232 rate itself is unchanged and verified at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives. The mechanical effect is to support regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border while suppressing the volume that crosses. Because premium assessments are periodic rather than daily, this will become measurable only at the next dated US Midwest mark, and nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of it.
drivers.source: Department of Finance Canada - list of US products subject to counter-tariffs effective 8-September-2026

prices.note: Carried at its last dated public assessment; NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK PRINTED INTO THE 09-SEPTEMBER COMPILE WINDOW and nothing has been interpolated or estimated. THE ASSESSMENT DATE IS SHOWN ON THE ROW SO THE STALENESS IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN IMPLIED. THE PUBLIC FORWARD VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE MOST USEFUL PART OF THIS PANEL: SMM expects the SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE, describing a market entering September in surplus with high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup keeping absolute prices under pressure. THE STRUCTURAL READ IS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: the refinery side of the chain remains in surplus while the smelter side is disrupted, and Alunorte has ramped back to full capacity from its August 50% cut on a TEMPORARY terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier. WHAT CHANGED THIS RUN IS NOT THE MARK BUT THE FRAGILITY OF THAT ARRANGEMENT, and the evidence sits on the macro panel rather than here: the agreement is a gas arrangement, and crude rose to a three-month high with Brent above $98 on renewed US-Iran escalation while European gas firmed 2.29% for a second consecutive session, a cumulative 4.2%. A TEMPORARY GAS ACCOMMODATION IS MORE FRAGILE IN A TIGHTENING GAS MARKET THAN IN A LOOSENING ONE, so the single largest identifiable upside risk to alumina - and therefore the largest downside risk to smelter margin - is modestly higher this morning even though no alumina number moved. FOR A COST READER THE IMPORTANT NUANCE THIS MONTH IS THAT THE STACK IS MOVING TWO WAYS AT ONCE - SMM expects prebaked anode and aluminium fluoride prices to RISE over the same period, and the energy tape now pushes the same way as the auxiliaries, so a falling alumina headline does not by itself imply a falling total cash cost.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT WAS $98.70 AT THIS COMPILE, UP 1.58% AND THROUGH $98, WITH WTI AT $93.93, UP 2.68% AND AT A THREE-MONTH HIGH. ENERGY IS THE LARGEST SINGLE COST LINE IN A SMELTER AND THE MOST IMPORTANT MACRO ROW ON THIS PAGE FOR A COST READER, AND IT MOVED MATERIALLY THIS SESSION RATHER THAN DRIFTING. Trading Economics carried the moves under the headlines 'Crude Oil Rises to Over 3-Month High' and 'Brent Crude Tops $99'. THE RISE IS CONSISTENT WITH RENEWED US-IRAN ESCALATION AND AN UNRESOLVED STRAIT OF HORMUZ SITUATION RATHER THAN WITH DEMAND STRENGTH, which is the uncomfortable combination for this industry: THE SAME DISRUPTION THAT SUPPORTS THE METAL PRICE ALSO RAISES THE COST OF PRODUCING IT AND OF SHIPPING IT. This is the clearest example on the page of a single variable that is simultaneously bullish for revenue and bearish for margin, and the direction of the net effect depends entirely on how much of the cost is hedged and how much of the supply loss is permanent. A firm crude tape alongside two central banks facing tightening decisions inside eight days is mildly stagflationary in character, and that is the macro backdrop the 16-September Federal Reserve decision sits against.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF WAS EUR 74.99/MWh AT THIS COMPILE, UP 2.29%, AND IT HAS NOW FIRMED FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE RUN FROM EUR 71.96 TO EUR 73.22 TO EUR 74.99 - A CUMULATIVE 4.2% IN TWO SESSIONS. EUROPEAN GAS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON EUROPEAN SMELTER RESTART ECONOMICS AND THE REASON ROUGHLY HALF OF EU PRIMARY CAPACITY HAS SAT CURTAILED SINCE 2022. THE LEVEL MATTERS MORE THAN THE DAILY MOVE AND IT IS STILL HIGH ENOUGH TO KEEP MOST RESTART DECISIONS MARGINAL - which is precisely why Slovalco is being restarted with a Slovak government carbon-compensation agreement behind it rather than on merchant power alone, why Alcoa needed energy hedging through 2027 at San Ciprian, and why Portland needed secured power to mid-2035. GAS IS ALSO THE CHANNEL THROUGH WHICH THE GULF DISRUPTION REACHES EUROPEAN COST, since Middle East LNG scarcity and European gas pricing are linked, and the two-session firming here is consistent with the crude move rather than independent of it. A RISING GAS PRICE IS A DIRECT BRAKE ON THE EUROPEAN RESTART PIPELINE, which is one of the larger bearish items on this page, so this row cuts modestly bullish for the metal even as it cuts bearish for European margin.

WHAT MATTERS FOR THIS PAGE IS THAT BOTH MOVES ARE SMALL RELATIVE TO A 0.45% METAL MOVE, so the aluminium advance is priced in the metal on either reading. IF ANYTHING THE LME FIXING MAKES THE MOVE SLIGHTLY BETTER THAN IT LOOKS, because on that measure the metal rose against a marginally firmer dollar rather than being helped by a weaker one. THE FORWARD TENSION IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS LARGE: a hawkish Federal Reserve on 16-September would push this row decisively the other way, and a dollar-priced industrial metal carries a mechanical headwind from dollar strength that is entirely independent of its own supply and demand.

row.note: THE EURO WAS $1.16156 AT THIS COMPILE, DOWN 0.06%, AGAINST AN LME FIXING OF 1.16140 THAT ITSELF FELL FROM 1.16230. THE TWO AGREE ON DIRECTION HERE - the euro is marginally softer - WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS THE MORE RELIABLE CURRENCY READ THIS MORNING THAN THE DOLLAR INDEX. THIS ROW MATTERS FOR TWO REASONS. FIRST, IT IS THE CURRENCY ADJUSTMENT ON THE HEADLINE PRICE: aluminium rose 0.45% in dollars and, with the euro marginally weaker, European buyers saw slightly MORE than the full move in euro terms. SECOND, AND FAR LARGER, THE EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECIDES TOMORROW, THURSDAY 10-SEPTEMBER, WITH A QUARTER-POINT RISE FULLY PRICED after euro-area August inflation rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. A RISE THAT IS FULLY PRICED MOVES THIS ROW ONLY IF THE GUIDANCE SURPRISES, so the risk here is two-sided rather than directional: dovish framing alongside the rise would be read as the end of the cycle and would weaken the euro further, while any signal of a follow-up would extend the euro-area tightening path into 2027. This is the nearest dated macro event on the page and it lands inside twenty-four hours.

row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR WAS 4.807% AT THIS COMPILE AND TRADING ECONOMICS CARRIED IT IN ITS NEWS STREAM AS A MULTI-YEAR HIGH, ALONGSIDE THE GERMAN TEN-YEAR AT A FIFTEEN-YEAR HIGH AND THE FINNISH TEN-YEAR AT A SEVENTEEN-YEAR HIGH. THE SYNCHRONISED MOVE ACROSS THREE SOVEREIGN CURVES IS MORE INFORMATIVE THAN ANY ONE OF THEM AND IT SAYS THE TIGHTENING REPRICING IS GLOBAL RATHER THAN AMERICAN. THE LEVEL IS THE POINT RATHER THAN THE DAILY MOVE, AND IT IS THE SINGLE CLEANEST TRANSMISSION CHANNEL FROM MACRO INTO THIS INDUSTRY'S SUPPLY SIDE. Every curtailed smelter weighing a restart is discounting a long stream of future margin against a cost of capital anchored here, and every entry in the restart pipeline on this page - Slovalco, San Ciprian, Portland, Mt Holly, Al Taweelah - required a power solution and a financing decision first. A HIGHER DISCOUNT RATE IS A GENUINE BRAKE ON THE RESTART PIPELINE EVEN AS THE PIPELINE ITSELF WIDENS, which is the main reason the hawkish repricing of the last fortnight is not straightforwardly bearish for the metal. It is a headwind for the price and a support for the balance, and those two effects have opposite signs.

headlines.title: ALUMINIUM SETTLED AT $3,325.00 ON 08-SEPTEMBER, UP $15.00 OR 0.45%, THE HIGHEST CASH OFFICIAL SINCE 10-AUGUST, AND THE BACKWARDATION TRIPLED TO $6.00 - THE WIDEST SINCE 10-AUGUST. Three-month rose $11.00 to $3,319.00, its own highest since 11-August. This is the third consecutive higher cash settlement and a cumulative $32.50 advance from Friday's $3,292.50. THE STRUCTURE IS MORE INFORMATIVE THAN THE PRICE: the $6.00 backwardation breaks a six-session stretch in which the front of the curve sat within $2.00 of flat, and it widened against exchange stock that did not move by a single tonne. A curve paying more for prompt metal with no warehouse response is being bid by demand for units rather than by an inventory shift. THE MOVE IS METAL RATHER THAN CURRENCY, AND SLIGHTLY BETTER THAN IT LOOKS: the LME's own EUR/USD fixing eased from 1.16230 to 1.16140, a marginally FIRMER dollar, so the advance was made against a small currency headwind. THE SCALE CAVEAT IS KEPT IN VIEW: $6.00 on a $3,325 metal is eighteen-hundredths of one percent and the August average spread was a $1.60 contango, so this is one session outside the recent mean rather than a new regime.

THE CROSS-METAL COMPARISON THAT HAS BEEN UNFLATTERING TO ALUMINIUM FOR THREE WEEKS INVERTED IN A SINGLE SESSION, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT OBSERVATION ON THE BOARD. Yesterday zinc carried a $182.00 backwardation and copper $92.00 while aluminium paid $2.00, and this page argued that was the cleanest available evidence that aluminium's thirty-six-year inventory low was not translating into prompt scarcity. TODAY ZINC'S BACKWARDATION COLLAPSED TO $106.00 - cash fell $47.00 to $4,110.00 while three-month ROSE $29.00 to $4,004.00, with 2,275 tonnes delivered in, the largest zinc build of the window - AND COPPER'S COLLAPSED TO $32.00, because although copper cash rose $197.00 to a window high of $14,737.00, three-month rose $257.00, more. Nickel's contango narrowed $10.00 to $145.00 on a 264-tonne build. Lead's contango WIDENED to $47.00 while shedding 3,400 tonnes, the heaviest draw on the board. ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY METAL ON THE BOARD WHOSE CURVE TIGHTENED. ONE SESSION IS NOT A TREND AND THAT IS STATED PLAINLY, but the specific criticism this page has levelled repeatedly has now been answered by the same diagnostic that produced it.

LME ALUMINIUM STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 244,525 TONNES ON 08-SEPTEMBER - A PUBLISHED CHANGE OF EXACTLY ZERO FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION AND THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE PUBLISHED READING AT THE IDENTICAL NUMBER, covering 04-September, 07-September and 08-September. Across the fifteen published sessions from 18-August to 08-September stock has fallen from 246,925 to 244,525 tonnes: a draw of 2,400 tonnes in three weeks, or 160 tonnes per session, under 0.1% of the total. THE LEVEL AND THE FLOW POINT DIFFERENT WAYS AND THE GAP WIDENED AGAIN THIS SESSION. The thirty-six-year low is real and is repeatedly cited in public commentary as a core support for the price; the draw that produced it has now stopped for three consecutive readings. A market being drained does not look like this. WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW AND CUTS THE OTHER WAY: the curve tightened anyway, tripling its backwardation on completely static stock, which is the first evidence in this window that prompt demand can firm without the warehouse series moving. THE CONTRARY EVIDENCE IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai exchange inventories fell 3% week on week on their latest published mark, so the Chinese visible series is still tightening even as the London one sits perfectly still.

THE GULF ESCALATED AGAIN AND THE ENERGY TAPE MOVED WITH IT: CRUDE ROSE TO A THREE-MONTH HIGH WITH BRENT ABOVE $98 AND WTI UP 2.68%, ON RENEWED US-IRAN HOSTILITIES AND AN UNRESOLVED STRAIT OF HORMUZ SITUATION. Trading Economics carried the moves under the headlines 'Crude Oil Rises to Over 3-Month High' and 'Brent Crude Tops $99', and its aluminium commentary states that the latest escalation has raised uncertainty over the potential return of aluminium supplies from the Persian Gulf. THIS IS THE PILLAR OF THE BULL CASE THAT HAS NOT WEAKENED AND IT STRENGTHENED THIS SESSION. Gulf capacity loss is not a forecast - it is observable in published company disclosures: Qatalum is running at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a second Hydro force majeure outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, representing 19% of its 1,623,000-tonne capacity with no restart announced. THE EFFECT IS DELIBERATELY TWO-SIGNED AND SHOULD NOT BE SIMPLIFIED: the same disruption that supports the metal price raises the energy and freight cost of producing and moving it everywhere else.

TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS DECIDE INSIDE EIGHT DAYS, THE FIRST OF THEM TOMORROW, AND THE BOND MARKET IS NOW CORROBORATING THE TIGHTENING REPRICING ACROSS BORDERS. The European Central Bank decides THURSDAY 10-SEPTEMBER with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August inflation rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. The US Federal Reserve follows WEDNESDAY 16-SEPTEMBER, and after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 - with June and July revised up a combined 55,000, unemployment steady at 4.1% and participation rising to 61.6% - traders are pricing the possibility of a HIKE. THE NEW EVIDENCE THIS RUN IS IN THE SOVEREIGN CURVES: the US ten-year at 4.807% was carried as a multi-year high, the German ten-year at a fifteen-year high and the Finnish ten-year at a seventeen-year high, all on the same session. A SYNCHRONISED MOVE ACROSS THREE SOVEREIGN CURVES SAYS THE REPRICING IS GLOBAL RATHER THAN AMERICAN. Higher policy rates are a direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal and simultaneously raise the discount rate on every curtailed smelter weighing a restart, so the effect on price and the effect on the physical balance have opposite signs.

CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS ON US ALUMINIUM ARE NOW IN FORCE, HAVING TAKEN EFFECT YESTERDAY, 08-SEPTEMBER-2026. Canada is applying 15%, 25% and 50% tariffs on products drawn from those targeted by the US Section 338 and Section 232 measures, with each product's rate matched to the corresponding US rate. IN STEEL AND ALUMINIUM SPECIFICALLY, EXISTING CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS ROSE FROM 25% TO 50% to align with the US rate. The measures cover $27.6 billion of imports from the United States and more than 300 metals products and derivatives, including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and follow the US decision to impose 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS IS TAGGED MIXED RATHER THAN BULLISH: it taxes flows in BOTH directions across what is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade corridor in the world. It supports regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border by raising the cost of arbitraging between them, and it simultaneously suppresses the volume that actually crosses. THE MEASURABLE TEST IS THE NEXT DATED US MIDWEST ASSESSMENT, and because those assessments are periodic rather than daily, the effect will appear with a lag rather than immediately - which is why nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of it.

THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM NEGOTIATION REMAINS OPEN 18-22% BELOW THE Q3 RECORD AND A SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE SEARCH RETURNED NO NEWER DATED REPORT. Reuters reported on 02-September-2026, citing four sources involved in the talks, that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered Japanese buyers $310-$325 per tonne for October-December shipments, down 18% to 22% on the Q3 settlement of $395, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. The stated rationale is a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer premiums in Europe; concerns over Iran-related shipment disruption and strong Japanese semiconductor-related demand are cited as offsetting support. Talks began the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS THEREFORE HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED, because narrowing it without a newer dated source would be judgement dressed as data. ONE PIECE OF THIS RUN'S EVIDENCE CUTS AGAINST THE PRODUCERS' STATED RATIONALE: the offers were justified partly on Middle East progress, but the Gulf escalated again this session with crude at a three-month high, and the exchange curve tightened rather than loosened.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXPORTS ROSE 18.7% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY AND REMAIN THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISM RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE. Public commentary attributes the surge to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship metal out despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap, easing shortages created by the Middle East disruption. THIS IS THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THE PAGE for a reader focused on London inventories: the metal relieving the Western market is arriving as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for why a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a warehouse series that has not moved a tonne in three published readings. THE OUTPUT CEILING IS REAL AND THE EXPORT FLOW IS ALSO REAL; they are not contradictory. THE NUANCE THIS RUN IS THAT THIS ARGUMENT EXPLAINS THE FLAT INVENTORY BUT NOT THE TIGHTENING CURVE - if ample semi-finished metal were fully satisfying prompt demand, the front of the curve should not be tripling its backwardation on the same session.

ALUNORTE, THE WORLD'S LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA, REMAINS RAMPED BACK TO FULL CAPACITY AFTER ITS AUGUST CUT TO 50%, FOLLOWING A TEMPORARY TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER, AND NO CHANGE TO THAT ARRANGEMENT WAS PUBLISHED INTO THIS COMPILE WINDOW. THE WORD TEMPORARY IS THE WHOLE RISK AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Restored alumina supply relieves the largest purchased input in the smelter cost stack and therefore removes a cost-push support from the aluminium price, which is why this is tagged bearish for the metal even though it is operationally good news. THE RISK IS MARGINALLY HIGHER THIS RUN RATHER THAN UNCHANGED, and the reason is on the macro panel rather than this one: the agreement is a gas arrangement, and the Gulf escalated again this session with crude at a three-month high and European gas up 4.2% across two sessions. A temporary gas accommodation is more fragile in a tightening gas market than in a loosening one. IF THE ARRANGEMENT LAPSES THE EFFECT REVERSES SHARPLY, and this remains the single largest identifiable upside risk to alumina and therefore the largest downside risk to smelter margin on this page.

SMM EXPECTS THE SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE WHILE PREBAKED ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE PRICES BOTH RISE, PUSHING AUXILIARY MATERIAL COSTS UP. Entering September the alumina market is described as maintaining a surplus with high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup, keeping absolute prices under pressure. THE SPLIT IS THE POINT FOR A COST READER AND IT IS WHY THIS IS TAGGED MIXED RATHER THAN BEARISH: the single largest purchased input is easing while the carbon and bath lines are firming, so the direction of total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone. The September prebaked anode settlement is 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t on an acceptance basis. THE ENERGY TAPE NOW PUSHES THE SAME WAY AS THE AUXILIARIES RATHER THAN AGAINST THEM: crude at a three-month high and European gas up 4.2% in two sessions both raise the power and freight components of the stack, which tilts the balance of this row further away from the comfortable reading that falling alumina means falling cost.

THE RESTART PIPELINE KEEPS WIDENING ON PUBLIC, DATED SCHEDULES AND EVERY ENTRY SHARES ONE FEATURE. Hydro is restarting 75,000 tonnes at Slovalco in Slovakia, the first tranche of 175,000 tonnes total, after reaching an agreement with the Slovak government on carbon cost compensation, with production guided to begin in Q4-2026. Alcoa's San Ciprian smelter in Spain has restarted and is running close to full capacity after securing energy hedging through 2027, and Alcoa completed the restart of 15,000 tonnes of previously curtailed capacity at Portland in Australia during Q2-2026, plus one 31,000-tonne potline at Lista in Norway. Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015. THE COMMON FEATURE IS THAT A POWER SOLUTION CAME FIRST - a government agreement, a secured purchase agreement, or both - WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THIS WEEK'S BOND-MARKET REPRICING IS A REAL CONSTRAINT ON THE PIPELINE RATHER THAN A THEORETICAL ONE. With the US ten-year at a multi-year high, the German ten-year at a fifteen-year high and European gas firming for a second session, the hurdle rate and the operating cost of the next restart decision both rose on the same day.

THE SOURCE IS FULLY CONSISTENT THIS MORNING FOR THE FIRST TIME IN OVER A MONTH, AND THAT IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THE LAST FOUR RUNS ALL CARRIED A DISCLOSED CAVEAT. The English and cache-busted German overview pages both carry the 08-September board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings. AND ALL FIVE PER-METAL DAILY TABLES - ALUMINIUM, COPPER, NICKEL, ZINC AND LEAD - HAVE NOW CAUGHT UP TO 08-SEPTEMBER AND REPRODUCE THE OVERVIEW EXACTLY. No row required the arithmetic reconciliation disclosed on 07-September, and the stock identity nevertheless still balances five out of five to the tonne against the prior session plus published changes. THE INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK ALSO AGREES: Trading Economics recorded its aluminium reference at $3,326.65 on 08-September, up 0.46%, $1.65 from the LME cash official with the same direction and near-identical magnitude. THIS IS TAGGED MIXED RATHER THAN BULLISH BECAUSE IT IS AN OPERATIONAL FACT ABOUT THE PAGE RATHER THAN ABOUT THE MARKET, but it does mean every figure published this morning is directly verified against two independent presentations of the same source rather than derived.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 36.9% directional hit rate against a 68.5% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 0.98% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (103 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-06-12). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

CARRIED AT THE 26-AUGUST-2026 DISCLOSURE AND RE-DATED ONLY, BECAUSE NO NEWER COMPANY STATEMENT PRINTED IN THIS WINDOW. EGA confirmed 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 reduction cells restarted - a quarter of the smelter - after the March Iranian strike on the Khalifa Economic Zone forced an emergency shutdown of all EGA facilities at the site. All three production lines were re-energised between May and August and are being worked simultaneously to speed the recovery, with around 1,000 people involved. Chief Executive Abdulnasser Bin Kalban reiterated the company remains on track to restore FULL PRODUCTION IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 2027. The refinery continues at about 50% capacity and the new recycling plant is increasing output as planned with full output expected by the final quarter of this year; EGA states the pace of further alumina ramp-up will be determined by supply-chain considerations and the optimisation of its alumina sourcing strategy. WHY IT MATTERS TODAY: Al Taweelah is roughly 1.5 Mt/y of nameplate and Reuters puts Middle East capacity at about 9% of the global total, so a restart running to a published schedule is the single largest identified source of returning supply on this panel. It is also the specific fact that Reuters names - a positive progress report on Middle East production - as one of two reasons producers opened the Japanese Q4 premium round 18-22% lower.

The package covers $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars, and is described by the Canadian government as matching the US Section 338 tariffs dollar for dollar after the US imposed 50% on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective 22-August. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TARIFF HEADLINE: the Canada-United States corridor is by volume the most important primary-aluminium trade route in the world, and it is now taxed in BOTH directions rather than one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A PHYSICAL READER IS DECOUPLING RATHER THAN SIMPLE INFLATION - regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border are mechanically supported because arbitrage between them is more expensive, while the volume that actually crosses is suppressed, so the delivered price and the exchange benchmark drift further apart. THE SECOND ACTIVE DRIVER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL UNRESOLVED: the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over any return of Persian Gulf supply, and Middle East LNG scarcity on tanker disruption continues to constrain regional refining and smelting.

catalysts.text: EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK DECISION - TOMORROW, AND THE NEAREST DATED MACRO EVENT ON THE PAGE - WITH A 25 BASIS POINT RISE FULLY PRICED. Euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. BECAUSE THE RISE IS FULLY PRICED THE MARKET-MOVING CONTENT IS THE GUIDANCE, and the risk is two-sided: dovish framing would be read as the end of the cycle, any signal of a follow-up extends the tightening path into 2027. The European leg matters disproportionately here because European restart economics are already marginal on energy cost - TTF has firmed 4.2% across two sessions - and because the duty-unpaid premium must absorb the Russian import ban at year end.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE DATE IN THE NEAR TERM. August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with June and July revised up a combined 55,000, unemployment steady at 4.1% and participation up to 61.6%, and traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. THE OPEN QUESTION HAS FLIPPED FROM WHETHER THE FED CUTS TO WHETHER IT RAISES, and the bond market is now corroborating that across borders - the US ten-year at 4.807% a multi-year high, the German ten-year at a fifteen-year high and the Finnish ten-year at a seventeen-year high on the same session. Direct headwind for a dollar-priced metal; simultaneously a brake on the restart pipeline through the discount rate, so the net effect on the physical balance is ambiguous even where the effect on price is not.

WHETHER THE BACKWARDATION HOLDS AND WHETHER THE INVENTORY DRAW RESUMES - AND THESE ARE NOW TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS RATHER THAN ONE. The spread tripled to $6.00, the widest since 10-August, while stock stayed pinned at 244,525 tonnes for a third consecutive published reading. THE CONFIRMING COMBINATION IS A RESUMED DRAW ALONGSIDE A BACKWARDATION THAT HOLDS OR WIDENS; that would convert a one-session signal into a tightness regime. THE FALSIFYING COMBINATION IS EQUALLY CLEAR AND SHOULD BE watched with the same attention: the spread slipping back inside $2.00 while stock stays flat would mark this session as noise. Watch also whether aluminium retains the distinction it earned on 08-September as the only metal on the board whose curve tightened, or whether it rejoins zinc and copper in giving structure back.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM, NOW PLAUSIBLY DAYS AWAY. Producers including Rio Tinto and South32 opened at $310-$325 per tonne against the Q3 record of $395, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300. Talks began the week of 24-August and run through later this month. THE PENDING RANGE HERE IS HELD AT $290-325 AND HAS NOT BEEN NARROWED, for a seventh consecutive run, because no dated public report newer than 02-September printed. ONE INPUT TO THE TALKS MOVED AGAINST THE PRODUCERS THIS SESSION: their stated rationale cited Middle East progress and softer European premiums, but the Gulf escalated again with crude at a three-month high and the exchange curve tightened rather than loosened. The settlement remains the single clearest public read on Asian physical tightness available.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly on this cadence; the September anode settlement is already public at 5,730 RMB/t spot and 5,745 RMB/t acceptance, above August's 5,630, and coal tar pitch has not printed a newer mark since 13-August. SMM EXPECTS SEPTEMBER ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH TO RISE WHILE THE MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE DECLINES, so the cost stack is moving two ways at once. THE ENERGY TAPE NOW PUSHES WITH THE AUXILIARIES RATHER THAN AGAINST THEM - crude at a three-month high and European gas up 4.2% across two sessions - which makes the comfortable reading that falling alumina means falling cash cost less tenable this month than last.

THE FIRST MEASURABLE TEST OF CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS, WHICH TOOK EFFECT 08-SEPTEMBER AND RAISED CANADIAN COUNTER-TARIFFS ON US STEEL AND ALUMINIUM FROM 25% TO 50%. The mechanical expectation is support for regional delivered premiums on both sides of the border alongside suppressed cross-border volume. BECAUSE PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN DAILY, THE EFFECT WILL APPEAR WITH A LAG, and nothing has been written into the premium rows on the strength of the measure alone. The US Midwest duty-paid row is carried at $2,094/t, of which $1,662.50 is the arithmetic tariff leg at a verified 50% rate on the current $3,325 exchange price, leaving an implied market leg of $431.50.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - now under sixteen weeks away. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it, and at a last assessment of $485/t - below its own trailing average, with the published rationale for lower Q4 Japanese offers explicitly citing SOFTER European premiums - it is not currently behaving as though the event is coming. Either replacement units are already sourced, or the event is not yet priced; the assessment cadence is too slow to tell which. THE PRESSURE ON THE REPLACEMENT-SUPPLY SIDE INCREASED THIS RUN, with European gas up 4.2% across two sessions and the ECB tightening tomorrow, both of which narrow the room for European restarts to supply those units.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE STATUS CHANGED FROM PENDING TO LIVE. NORTH AMERICAN TRADE FRAGMENTATION IS NO LONGER A SCHEDULED EVENT - IT IS IN FORCE. Canada's counter-tariffs took effect on 08-September and explicitly include aluminium, with counter-tariffs on US steel and aluminium rising from 25% to 50% to match the US rate, inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports and more than 300 metals products and derivatives including flat-rolled steel and aluminium bars. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE, and it is now being tested in real time rather than anticipated. The largest primary-aluminium trade corridor in the world is taxed in both directions, which mechanically supports delivered premiums on both sides of the border while suppressing the volume that crosses and decoupling regional prices from the exchange benchmark. THE US SECTION 232 RATE ITSELF WAS RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN AND IS UNCHANGED AT 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES. IT IS HELD AT UP RATHER THAN RAISED FURTHER FOR AN HONEST REASON: the measure is now known and quantified, so the incremental risk from here is further escalation rather than this event, and the effect will only become measurable at the next dated US Midwest assessment.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE CHANGE ON NEW EVIDENCE RATHER THAN DRIFT. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. The pipeline itself is unchanged and remains substantial: Slovalco is restarting the first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 tonnes total under a Slovak government carbon-cost compensation agreement, guided to begin in Q4-2026; Alcoa's San Ciprian has restarted close to full on energy hedging through 2027, with Portland's 15,000 tonnes completed in Q2-2026 and a 31,000-tonne Lista potline restarted; Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015; EGA has 315 of Al Taweelah's 1,262 cells back online with pre-war output reaffirmed for Q1-2027. WHAT CHANGED IS THE GATING CONDITION, AND BOTH HALVES OF IT WORSENED ON THE SAME SESSION. Every entry in that pipeline required a power solution and a financing decision first. On 08-September the US ten-year printed at 4.807% and was carried as a multi-year high, the German ten-year at a fifteen-year high and the Finnish ten-year at a seventeen-year high, while European gas TTF firmed 2.29% for a second consecutive session, a cumulative 4.2%. THE HURDLE RATE AND THE OPERATING COST OF THE NEXT RESTART DECISION BOTH ROSE ON THE SAME DAY, so the risk of faster-than-expected return has stopped increasing even though the announced pipeline has not shrunk.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND CORROBORATED BY NEW CROSS-BORDER EVIDENCE. MACRO TIGHTENING RISK REMAINS THE CLEAREST NEAR-TERM PRICE HEADWIND AND THE FIRST OF TWO DATED DECISIONS LANDS TOMORROW. The European Central Bank decides Thursday 10-September with a 25 basis point rise fully priced after euro-area August CPI rebounded to 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023. The US Federal Reserve follows Wednesday 16-September after August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, with prior months revised up a combined 55,000 and participation rising to 61.6%; traders moved to price the possibility of a HIKE. WHAT IS NEW THIS RUN IS THAT THE BOND MARKET IS NOW CONFIRMING THE REPRICING ACROSS THREE SOVEREIGN CURVES SIMULTANEOUSLY: the US ten-year at 4.807% carried as a multi-year high, the German ten-year at a fifteen-year high and the Finnish ten-year at a seventeen-year high, all on the same session. A SYNCHRONISED MOVE ACROSS THREE MARKETS SAYS THE TIGHTENING IS GLOBAL RATHER THAN AMERICAN, which removes the usual offset in which a hawkish Fed is cushioned for non-dollar buyers by a dovish elsewhere. For a dollar-priced industrial metal this is a direct headwind, and the second-order effect cuts the other way by raising the discount rate on every restart decision.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND IT ESCALATED AGAIN, VISIBLY, IN THE ENERGY TAPE. THE MIDDLE EAST DISRUPTION REMAINS THE ONE PILLAR OF THE BULL CASE THAT HAS NOT WEAKENED. Crude rose to a three-month high on the 08-September session with Brent above $98, up 1.58%, and WTI up 2.68%, which Trading Economics attributes to renewed US-Iran escalation; its aluminium commentary states that the latest escalation has raised uncertainty over the potential return of aluminium supplies from the Persian Gulf, and that Middle East LNG supply, essential for refining, has been scarce on tanker disruption in the Strait. THE UNDERLYING CAPACITY LOSS IS OBSERVABLE IN PUBLIC COMPANY DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN INFERRED: Qatalum is at roughly 60% of its 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas with a second Hydro force majeure on aluminium sales outstanding, and Aluminium Bahrain has had reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March 2026, 19% of 1,623,000 tonnes, with no restart announced. NEITHER HAS A PUBLISHED RESOLUTION DATE, which is what distinguishes them from the scheduled restart pipeline. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED: the same escalation raises the energy and freight cost of producing and moving metal everywhere else, so it is bullish for price and bearish for margin at the same time.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND THE FRAGILITY INCREASED WITHOUT ANY ALUMINA NUMBER MOVING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN. Alunorte, the world's largest alumina refinery outside China, is back at full capacity from its August cut to 50% ON A TEMPORARY TERMINAL-ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER. The word temporary is the whole exposure. WHAT CHANGED THIS RUN IS THE ENVIRONMENT AROUND THAT AGREEMENT: it is a gas arrangement, and the gas market tightened on the 08-September session, with crude at a three-month high on renewed US-Iran escalation and European TTF up 2.29% for a second consecutive session, a cumulative 4.2%. A TEMPORARY GAS ACCOMMODATION IS MORE FRAGILE IN A TIGHTENING GAS MARKET THAN IN A LOOSENING ONE. SMM SEPARATELY EXPECTS THE SEPTEMBER MONTHLY AVERAGE ALUMINA PRICE TO DECLINE on surplus, high operating capacity and continued inventory buildup, WHILE PREBAKED ANODE AND ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE BOTH RISE, and the firming energy tape now pushes the same way as the auxiliaries rather than against them. THE COST STACK IS MOVING IN AT LEAST THREE DIRECTIONS AT ONCE and total cash cost is not readable from the alumina headline alone. Bauxite remains the least-watched and most geographically concentrated link, with roughly two tonnes of alumina required per tonne of metal, so a bauxite disruption propagates with a lag.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO FLAT ON A SPECIFIC PIECE OF COUNTER-EVIDENCE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CHINESE EXPORT SUPPLY RELIEVES THE WESTERN SHORTAGE FASTER THAN THE BALANCE FORECASTS ASSUME, AND IT REMAINS THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED BEARISH FACT ON THIS PAGE. Exports rose 18.7% year on year in July, with public commentary attributing the surge to muted domestic demand allowing producers to ship out despite Beijing's 45-million-tonne output cap. The mechanism matters more than the number: the relieving metal arrives as semi-finished and alloy product that does not pass through LME warehouses, which is one coherent explanation for how a thirty-six-year exchange inventory low can coexist with a warehouse series that has not moved a tonne in three published readings. TWO THINGS ARGUE AGAINST RAISING IT FURTHER THIS RUN. FIRST, THERE IS NO NEWER DATA - the July export figure is the latest public print and it has been carried unchanged for several runs, so any increase would be drift rather than evidence. SECOND, AND MORE INTERESTINGLY, THE 08-SEPTEMBER CURVE ARGUES AGAINST THE STRONG FORM OF THIS THESIS: if ample Chinese semi-finished metal were fully satisfying Western prompt demand, the front of the aluminium curve should not have tripled its backwardation on the same session. The export flow explains the flat inventory; it does not explain the tightening curve.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE UNDERLYING FACT GOT WORSE EVEN AS ITS CONSEQUENCE GOT MORE AMBIGUOUS. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. Exchange stock was UNCHANGED at 244,525 tonnes on 08-September - a published change of exactly ZERO for the SECOND consecutive session and the THIRD consecutive published reading at the identical number - and has fallen just 2,400 tonnes across the fifteen sessions from 18-August to 08-September, about 160 tonnes per session. LEVEL AND FLOW HAVE SEPARATED FURTHER, NOT LESS: the thirty-six-year low is real and remains the strongest single support for the price, but the draw that produced it has now stopped for three consecutive readings. A market being drained does not look like this. THE REASON THIS IS HELD AT UP RATHER THAN RAISED IS THE ONE PIECE OF GENUINE COUNTER-EVIDENCE THIS RUN: the curve tightened anyway, tripling its backwardation to $6.00 on completely static stock, which suggests the bull case may not depend on the inventory flow as exclusively as this risk assumes. THE PRACTICAL READ IS UNCHANGED: until the London flow resumes, the inventory statistic should be treated as a floor under the price rather than as a trigger for the next leg higher. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS REPORTED FOR BALANCE: Shanghai inventories fell 3% week on week, so the two visible series still disagree.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM FLAT TO DOWN - THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE RE-RATING THIS RUN, AND IT IS MADE ON THE SAME DIAGNOSTIC THAT PRODUCED THE ORIGINAL CONCERN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. Cash settled $6.00 ABOVE three-month on 08-September, a BACKWARDATION that TRIPLED from $2.00 and is the WIDEST SINCE 10-AUGUST, breaking a six-session run in which the front of the curve had been pinned within $2.00 of flat. IT WIDENED ON EXCHANGE STOCK THAT DID NOT MOVE BY A SINGLE TONNE, which is the first evidence in this window that prompt demand can firm without the warehouse series moving. THE CROSS-METAL DIAGNOSTIC THAT WAS THE BASIS OF THIS RISK HAS INVERTED: for three weeks this page argued that zinc's $182.00 and copper's $92.00 backwardations showed what a curve genuinely paying for prompt metal looks like, and that aluminium was not doing it. On this session zinc's collapsed to $106.00 on a 2,275-tonne build and copper's to $32.00, while nickel and lead stayed in contango, and ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY METAL ON THE BOARD WHOSE CURVE TIGHTENED. THE RATING IS LOWERED TO DOWN RATHER THAN RESOLVED, AND THE RESTRAINT IS DELIBERATE: $6.00 on a $3,325 metal is still only eighteen-hundredths of one percent, the August average spread was a $1.60 contango, and this is one session. The signal has become actionable information rather than noise; it has not yet become a regime.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026 AND IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE - now under sixteen weeks away. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS A DISORDERLY EUROPEAN SUPPLY RESET. The European duty-unpaid premium is the price that must absorb it and it is NOT BEHAVING AS IF THE EVENT IS COMING: duty-unpaid was last assessed at $485/t, below its own trailing average, and the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese producer offers explicitly cites SOFTER premiums in Europe. TWO READINGS ARE LIVE AND THE ASSESSMENT CADENCE IS TOO SLOW TO DISTINGUISH THEM: either the market has already sourced replacement units and the ban is priced, or the event is not yet in the price at all. The second reading is the risk, and it becomes harder to hedge the closer the date comes. THE SECOND-ORDER PRESSURE INCREASED THIS RUN: European gas firmed for a second consecutive session, a cumulative 4.2%, and the European Central Bank decides tomorrow - so the region that must absorb a supply shock at year end is simultaneously facing rising energy cost and a tightening policy rate, which narrows the room for European restarts to supply the replacement units.

RE-ASSESSED 09-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN AND IT IMPROVED FURTHER - THIS IS THE CLEANEST SOURCE STATE THE PAGE HAS RECORDED IN OVER A MONTH. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the public price source this page depends on fails to publish, publishes stale cached snapshots, or disagrees with itself. THIS MORNING IT DID NONE OF THOSE THINGS. The English and cache-busted German overview pages both carry the 08-September board and agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings, AND ALL FIVE PER-METAL DAILY TABLES HAVE CAUGHT UP TO 08-SEPTEMBER AND REPRODUCE THE OVERVIEW EXACTLY. NO ROW REQUIRED THE ARITHMETIC RECONCILIATION THAT EACH OF THE LAST FOUR RUNS DISCLOSED - every figure published this morning is directly verified against two independent presentations of the same source. The stock identity nevertheless still balances five out of five to the tonne, and the independent Trading Economics reference at $3,326.65 sits $1.65 from the LME cash official with the same direction. IT IS HELD AT DOWN RATHER THAN CLOSED FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON: the page still depends on a single primary price source, and the intermittent caching and publication-lag failures observed on 31-July, 04-August and across late August and early September were characteristics of that source rather than one-off events. A clean morning is evidence the controls work, not evidence the exposure has gone.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity.
